name: Hardy Storage Company pipeline

values.EndLocation: Columbia Gas Transmission system, Hampshire County

researcher_notes: A Federal Register notice of 12 August 2005 for the FERC environmental assessment says Hardy Storage Company LLC would install about 36.8 miles of natural gas transmission pipeline in Hardy and Hampshire Counties, West Virginia. A Natural Gas Intelligence article on the FERC certificate gives 36.9 miles, including a new 13 mile 20-inch line joining the field to Columbia's system (supports length within rounding; not cited in a ref cell since it is not independent of the same FERC order). A Natural Gas Intelligence article dated 3 April 2007 says the storage facility came on-line, which supports operating and a 2007 start; its body text could not be checked for the pipeline. The 36.8 miles is the planned figure and covers field lines of mixed size (12 and 20 inch per court filings), so diameter is left blank and the as-built length is not confirmed. No GEM row exists for Hardy or Hampshire County West Virginia. Owner is a joint venture of Columbia Gas Transmission and Piedmont Natural Gas subsidiaries; Columbia operates. Ownership team style for the name was a medium-confidence suggestion of 'Hardy Storage Co', not an exact gazetteer hit, so the name is kept as the source spells it. Capacity (176,000 Dth/d is the storage deliverability, not pipe capacity) left blank. Route not researched; suggest a FERC GIS or state map search later. The Columbia Virginia loops are a separate candidate. Passes the 25 km rule: 36.8 mi is about 59 km.
